342580.title: Projection conjecture for large arcs and common zeros of quadrics
342580.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be an arc of size $2k+3$ in $\mathrm{PG}(k-1,{\mathbb F})$, and let $U$ be the subspace of quadratic forms that vanish on $X$. If

$$
\dim U \geqslant {k-1 \choose 2}-1,
$$

then **projection conjecture.** The projection of $V(U)$ to $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$ from any $k-4$ points of $V(U)$ is contained in the intersection of two linearly independent quadratic forms. The conjecture extends the paper's observed examples, most of which project onto intersections of two quadrics; the supplied text does not indicate whether it has been resolved.
342580.reason: Projection of a quadric ideal needs an elimination/dimension argument uniform over every allowed center. Arc hypothesis and target field notation require primary repair; no such mechanism supplied.

342672.title: The degree-sequence conjecture for hat guessing
342672.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with degree sequence $(d_1,d_2,\dots,d_n)$, and let a sequence be **winning** for $G$ when it gives the corresponding hat-guessing game a winning strategy. **Degree-sequence conjecture.** The sequence $(d_1,d_2,\dots,d_n)$ is winning for $G$.

This conjecture proposes that the degrees themselves always provide a winning sequence. The paper notes that for $C_5$, the sequence $(d_1+1,\ldots,d_5+1)$ is not winning, illustrating that increasing every degree by one does not preserve the analogous property.
342672.reason: Winning sequence depends on heterogeneous game conventions and possible isolated vertices. Degree-zero endpoint is not a source-qualified counterexample; old Hat formal bodies were not accessed. No full mechanism.

342704.title: Conjecture on group distance magic labelings of Cartesian products of cycles
342704.literal_statement:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers such that $mn$ is even, let $\Gamma$ be an Abelian group of order $mn$, and let $r=\exp(\Gamma)$ be its exponent. For a positive integer $k$, write $f(k)$ for the greatest divisor of $k$ that is a power of $2$. Then

**Conjecture on Cartesian products of cycles.** The Cartesian product $C_m\square C_n$ admits a $\Gamma$-distance magic labeling if and only if

$$
2r\min\{f(m),f(n),\mathop{\rm gcd}\nolimits(m,n)\}\geq\operatorname{lcm}(m,n).
$$

This conjecture proposes a complete criterion for group distance magic labelings of Cartesian products of two cycles. The paper derives necessary conditions and proves the criterion in some cases, but presents the full characterization as an open problem.

342737.title: Iosevich's sum-product conjecture over prime fields
342737.literal_statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{F}_p$, and let $\epsilon>0$. **Iosevich's conjecture.** If

$$
|A|\gg p^{\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon},
$$

then

$$
A\cdot A+A\cdot A=\mathbb{F}_p,\qquad (A-A)^2+(A-A)^2=\mathbb{F}_p.
$$

The conjecture concerns simultaneous additive-multiplicative expansion in prime fields and is stated after a theorem giving a weaker exponent for related product-set conclusions; the source does not state a resolution status.
342737.reason: Prime-field asymptotic quantifier requires both covering conclusions with a uniform constant depending on epsilon; a small prime or density-one argument cannot settle it.

342765.title: Conjecture on the α-spectral radius of hypertrees in NC(m,d)
342765.literal_statement:
Let $NC(m,d)$ be the class of hypertrees with $m$ edges and diameter $d$, let $H_1(m,d)$ be the specified extremal hypertree, and let $\rho_{\alpha}$ denote the α-spectral radius. Assume $0\leq\alpha<1$.

**The $NC(m,d)$ extremal conjecture.** For $G\in NC(m,d)$,

$$
\rho_{\alpha}(G)\leq\rho_{\alpha}(H_1(m,d)).
$$

Equality holds if and only if $G\cong H_1(m,d)$.
This conjecture would identify $H_1(m,d)$ uniquely as the maximizer of the α-spectral radius in $NC(m,d)$. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
342765.reason: NC and H1 are source-defined; uniqueness for every alpha requires a global spectral transformation preserving diameter and class. No paid extremal mechanism.

342776.title: Low-dimensional modularity conjecture for graph $c_2$-invariants
342776.literal_statement: A $c_2$-invariant has a dimension determined by the minimal model, and it is called modular when its sequence is associated with a modular form. Graphs are classified as $\phi^4$ or non-$\phi^4$ according to their vertex valences. **Low-dimensional modularity conjecture.** Every $\phi^4$ $c_2$-invariant of dimension $2$ or $3$ is modular, no $\phi^4$ $c_2$-invariant has dimension $1$, and every non-$\phi^4$ $c_2$-invariant of dimension $1$ or $2$ is modular. The claim reflects observed modular behavior in low dimensions, while the general assertions remain open.
342776.reason: References say refuted while literal statement says open, but no applicable refutation body read; cannot turn conflicting metadata into exclusion.

342837.title: Homology concentration conjecture for nucleus complexes
342837.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph and let $U\subseteq V(G)$. Write $\Delta^G_U$ for the nucleus complex associated with $G$ and $U$, and let $\widetilde H_k(\Delta^G_U;\mathbb{R})$ denote its reduced homology group in degree $k$.

**Homology concentration conjecture.** The group $\widetilde H_k(\Delta^G_U;\mathbb{R})$ is nonzero only in the following cases:

$$
\text{(i) } U=\varnothing\text{ and } k=|E(G)|-|V(G)|-1,
$$

or

$$
\text{(ii) } |U|\geq 2\text{ and } k=|E(G)|-|V(G)|.
$$

This conjecture concerns the homological structure of nucleus complexes. The source says that experimental data gathered using Sage supports it, but supplies no proof or resolution, so the assertion remains open.
342837.reason: Need nucleus definition and a uniform homotopy/Morse mechanism for all G,U; Euler characteristic positivity does not prove concentration. No primary body read.

342871.title: The relative hyperbolicity classification conjecture for hierarchical twist-free graphs of multicurves
342871.literal_statement:
A **hierarchical, twist-free graph of multicurves** is a graph $d4a2$ equipped with the hierarchical structure described in the paper, with no twists. The associated HHS structure is the one constructed for $d4a2$ in Theorem described in the source.

**Relative hyperbolicity classification conjecture.** $d4a2$ is relatively hyperbolic if and only if this HHS structure has isolated orthogonality.

This conjecture would characterize relative hyperbolicity directly from the natural HHS structure of a hierarchical, twist-free graph of multicurves. The preceding discussion establishes only that isolated orthogonality is a sufficient condition, so the converse remains open.
342871.reason: Placeholder d4a2 and unnamed theorem leave source bridge unpaid; sufficient isolated-orthogonality implication alone does not prove converse.

342880.title: Benjamini's conjecture on expanders at all scales
342880.literal_statement: An infinite, connected, bounded-degree graph $\mathcal G$ is an **expander at all scales** if there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that every ball $B\subset \mathcal G$ and subset $A\subset \mathcal G$ with $|A\cap B|\leq |B|/2$ satisfy $|\partial A\cap B|\geq\varepsilon|A\cap B|$. **Benjamini's conjecture.** Expanders at all scales do not exist. The paper proves the analogue for random walks, showing that no infinite graph can have heat-kernel-weighted subgraphs forming an expander family; the metric-ball formulation stated here is the conjectural one.
342880.reason: Heat-kernel expansion and metric-ball expansion are distinct quantifiers. No transfer giving the full infinite bounded-degree nonexistence.

342955.title: The gated-hull characterization conjecture for two-dimensional partial cubes
342955.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a partial cube, and for each isometric cycle of $G$ consider its gated hull. A gated hull is a **disk** or a **full subdivision** according to the corresponding classes of cell complexes described in the paper.

**Gated-hull characterization conjecture.** If the gated hull of each isometric cycle of $G$ is a disk or a full subdivision, then $G$ is two-dimensional.

This conjecture asserts that condition (vii) in the characterization theorem is equivalent to conditions (i)--(vi), thereby giving a local characterization of two-dimensional partial cubes. The paper does not provide a proof or resolution of this converse implication.
342955.reason: Disk/full subdivision/gated hull and dimension require primary definitions. No all-cycle local-to-global mechanism paid.

342960.title: Gamma-positivity conjecture for symmetric edge polytopes of type A
342960.literal_statement: Let ${\mathcal A}_G$ be a symmetric edge polytope of type A, and let $h^*({\mathcal A}_G,x)$ denote its $h^*$-polynomial. **Type A symmetric edge-polytope conjecture.** The $h^*$-polynomial of any symmetric edge polytope of type A is $\gamma$-positive. The conjecture is motivated by the preceding explicit calculations for complete bipartite graphs; its general status is not resolved in the supplied source.
342960.reason: Gamma positivity for all symmetric edge polytopes needs coefficient/nonnegative decomposition; complete-bipartite cases do not prove general claim.

343074.title: Partite-set comparison conjecture for expected propagation times of complete bipartite graphs
343074.literal_statement:
Let $K_{m,n}$ have partite vertex sets $R$ and $R'$ of orders $m$ and $n$ respectively, and let $u\in R$ and $v\in R'$. **Partite-set comparison conjecture.** If $n>3$ and $m<n$, then

$$
\operatorname{ept}(K_{m,n},\{u\})>\operatorname{ept}(K_{m,n},\{v\}).
$$

The conjecture asserts that, except for the noted small outlier, starting from a vertex in the larger partite set gives a smaller expected propagation time. Its status is not established in the supplied material.

343104.title: Unique permutation with maximal stabilization
343104.literal_statement:
Let $w$ be a permutation of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, viewed as a tableau, and let $\stab(w)$ denote its stabilization time. **Maximal-stabilization conjecture.** The increasing permutation

$$
w=1\,2\,\dots\,(n-1)\,n
$$

is the only permutation with $\stab(w)=n$. This asks for the rightmost entry in the stabilization distribution on permutations to be unique. The statement is posed as an open problem after the paper notes that the leftmost entry is always $1$; its truth is not established there.
343104.reason: Stabilization depends on source tableau dynamics; no definition-level endpoint or proof of uniqueness read. Not excluded as routine.

343192.title: Non-biregular construction conjecture for critical bipartite graphs
343192.literal_statement:
Let $n,m,k$ be positive integers such that $1<m<n$ and $k=n-m$. Set

$$
a=\frac{m(n-m+1)}{n}
$$

and suppose that $a$ is not an integer. Let $a'=\lceil a\rceil$, and define

$$
U=\{u_i\mid i\in[n]\},\qquad V=\{v_j\mid j\in[m]\},
$$

$$
E=\{(u_i,v_{(j+\alpha)\bmod m})\mid i\in[n],\ \alpha\in[a'],\ j=\lceil im/n\rceil\}.
$$

**Non-biregular construction conjecture.** The graph $(U,V;E)$ is $k$-critical bipartite.

This conjecture proposes a construction extending the paper's biregular construction to unbalanced bipartite graphs that are not biregular. The source presents it as work in progress and gives no resolution.

343220.title: The toroidal graph without configurations in E DP-4-degeneracy conjecture
343220.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a toroidal graph with no subgraph isomorphic to any configuration in the family denoted by $E$. Let $(H,f)$ be a cover of $G$, where $f$ assigns to each vertex of $H$ a value in $\{0,1,2\}$. A **strictly $f$-degenerate transversal** is a transversal of $H$ inducing, in every nonempty subgraph, a vertex whose degree is less than its assigned $f$-value. **The toroidal graph without configurations in $E$ conjecture.** If

$$
f(v,1)+f(v,2)+\dots+f(v,\kappa)\geq 4
$$

for each $v\in V(G)$, then $H$ has a strictly $f$-degenerate transversal. The known theorem for a more restricted family of forbidden configurations motivates this proposed extension; its truth is not established in the supplied text.
343220.reason: Forbidden family E includes material configurations not acquired. A planar coloring theorem would not cover toroidal arbitrary covers with f in {0,1,2}.

343221.title: The planar and toroidal graphs without intersecting triangles DP-4-degeneracy conjecture
343221.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a planar or toroidal graph without intersecting triangles. Let $(H,f)$ be a cover of $G$, where $f$ assigns to each vertex of $H$ a value in $\{0,1,2\}$. A **strictly $f$-degenerate transversal** is a transversal of $H$ inducing, in every nonempty subgraph, a vertex whose degree is less than its assigned $f$-value. **The planar and toroidal graphs without intersecting triangles conjecture.** If

$$
f(v,1)+f(v,2)+\dots+f(v,\kappa)\geq 4
$$

for each $v\in V(G)$, then $H$ has a strictly $f$-degenerate transversal. This conjecture extends established DP-colouring, list-colouring, and vertex-arboricity results for planar and toroidal graphs without intersecting triangles; the full cover statement remains open.
343221.reason: Ordinary/list coloring does not supply strictly f-degenerate transversals for all covers; a uniform toroidal structural reduction is unpaid.

343225.title: The independence number conjecture for even Johnson-type graphs $J_{\pm}(n,4,1)$
343225.literal_statement:
Let $J_{\pm}(n,4,1)$ be the Johnson-type graph with parameters $n$, $4$, and $1$, and let $\alpha[G]$ denote the independence number of a graph $G$. **Independence number conjecture.** Let $n>n_0$ be an even number. Then

$$
\alpha[J_{\pm}(n,4,1)]=2n(n-2).
$$

This is posed as an open question about determining independence numbers of Johnson-type graphs; the source does not provide a proof or resolution for this parameter range.
343225.reason: Threshold n0 and all sufficiently large even n cannot be settled by a fixed witness. Need source signed-vector adjacency and uniform independent-set upper bound.

343280.title: Type-1 zero-problem conjecture for 3M-DAPs
343280.literal_statement:
Let $P=(T;U,V)$ be a 3M-DAP. Write $t,u,v$ for the relevant row lengths, $s_t,s_u,s_v$ for the numbers of rows of types $T,U,V$, and $x_t,x_u,x_v$ for their total values. A $(T,V)$-pair consists of subsets of $T$- and $V$-rows with sizes $a$ and $b$.

**Type-1 zero-problem conjecture.** If $s_t\leq(v-1)s_v$, then the optimal solution consists of $(T,V)$-pairs with $a/b=s_t/s_v$, with $(T,V)$ itself being one such pair, and the optimal value is

$$
\frac{s_tx_t-s_vx_v}{s_tt-s_vv}=\frac{x_u}{u},
$$

i.e. all values in $U$ must be $x_u/u$.

The source presents this as a conjecture about the structure and value of optimal solutions for this class of 3M-DAPs. No resolution is supplied in the stated context.
343280.reason: Row/value feasibility and optimality conventions not sourced; balancing equality alone proves neither all optimizers structure nor feasibility.

343287.title: The gradedness conjecture for Q-Bruhat posets
343287.literal_statement:
Let $Q
i\operatorname{POS}(n)$ and $k\in[n]$. For each $I\in Q^k_B(\mathbb{C})$, let $[Q]_I(\mathbb{C})$ denote the associated incidence stratum, and let $\dim([Q]_I(\mathbb{C}))$ be its dimension. **The gradedness conjecture.** The poset $(Q^k_B(\mathbb{C}),\subseteq)$ is graded with rank function

$$
\rho(I)=\dim([Q]_I(\mathbb{C})).
$$

This conjecture proposes that the incidence stratification has a rank compatible with inclusion, extending the graded structure observed in the classical Bruhat setting. Its resolution is not given in the source.
343287.reason: Incidence-stratum definitions and closure inclusion are unpaid. Dimension difference along every cover needs a source-defined degeneration argument.

343288.title: The gradedness conjecture for mixed Q-P flag posets
343288.literal_statement:
Let $n>0$, let $k\in[n]$, and let $Q,P\in\operatorname{POS}(n)$. Consider the poset $(Q^P_B(\mathbb{C}),\subseteq)$. **The gradedness conjecture.** The poset $(Q^P_B(\mathbb{C}),\subseteq)$ is graded.

This conjecture asserts gradedness for the more general posets arising from pairs of posets $Q$ and $P$, extending the preceding $Q$-Bruhat gradedness question. The source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
343288.reason: Arbitrary Q,P generalized flag-poset gradedness has no paid cover-length mechanism; classic Bruhat grading is insufficient.
